newsitem.title: SYRIA: Assad says Syria still committed to peace.
newsitem.headline: Assad says Syria still committed to peace.

text.p: President Hafez al-Assad has said Syria is still committed to peace with Israel as a strategic option but accused the current Jewish government of responsbility for the existing stalemate.

"Syria is committed to a just and comprehensive peace as a strategic option. Syria worked to achieve this peace on the basis of land-for-peace," Assad said at a dinner in Damascus on Sunday in honour of visiting President Cheddi Jagan of Guyana.
"A just and comprehensive peace would provide security and stability to the region. It provides the appropriate climate for economic development," Assad said.
Syria in September redeployed some 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some to within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights. This spurred war jitters in Israel.

Natan Sharansky, a former Soviet Jewish dissident who became Israel's minister of trade and industry, urged the Israeli government in an interview published on Sunday to prepare the public for war with Syria.
"In light of the Syrian threats, and they are very serious in my opinion, the best way is to begin preparing people for the possibility of war," Sharansky told Israel's daily Haaretz.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said later Israel should be prepared but hoped for calm.

"We have an interest in calm. We have no aims across the border. We are taking preparedness and alertness steps. I appeal to Assad and the Syrians to return to the negotiating table," Mordechai told a news conference during a visit to Israel's border with Lebanon.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but with little progress.

Damascus has strongly condemned the refusal of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who came to power in June elections, to trade occupied Arab lands for peace. It says it will not resume talks until he declares readiness to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.
Assad said the current Israeli government should also honour the commitments that were made by the previous Labour-led cabinet which adopted the principle of land-for-peace.
"The current Israeli government reversed the commitments of the previous government and insisted on returning the peace process to the zero point," Assad said.

He praised the efforts exerted by France and Russia to revive Arab-Israeli peace talks and said the Russian and French roles complemented that of the United States which is co-sponsoring the negotiations.

French President Jacques Chirac visited Syria and Israel as part of a regional tour last month and demanded a more active European role in Arab-Israeli negotiations, co-sponsored by the U.S. and Russia. But his demand was refused by Israel.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov also visited Syria and Israel and was reported to have passed on messages by both sides that neither was preparing for war.
